title: Fail closed: a demoted finding must never exit 0
note: TDD. Red first: the CLI unit test failed with enforcementDegradedByCompleteness is not a function, and the e2e failed with expected 3, received 0 - the exact red the plan specifies. Both green now. Refusal names the causing file; the control (violation alone, complete coverage) still exits 2, so no over-refusal.
evidence: Reproduced the defect on test/fixtures/enforcement-gate-adjacent with NO harness involved: a new violating route alone exits 2 with enforcement_result block; add an adjacent route whose only content is a namespace import of a real workspace package and the same violation returns none and the check exits 0. One detail the fixture had to get right - the degrading route must be IN THE DIFF, because the completeness gate only considers API-route files in the checked scope. My first fixture committed the adjacent route and the check correctly exited 2, which would have been a test that passed while the bug was fully present.
diagnosis: CORRECTED THE PLAN SEAM. It says derive the flag from checkData.completeness, which is already available. It is available but it is the SCAN completeness, and probing the repro showed it reports can_block true, complete true, reasons [] while the finding is already demoted - the demotion happens inside check-repo, whose completeness the CLI discards. Reading the scan would have shipped a fix that never fires. So the predicate detects the EFFECT: enforcement_result_for maps block to block unconditionally, therefore a block-mode convention carrying none can only have been zeroed. Exact, and needs no plumbing. Also corrects my own T101 reclassification - I generalised from the harness manufactured this instance to the behaviour is correct, and this is the test with a resolvable module that keeps it open.
